scope: Official Twitch documentation; no signed-in registration or real OAuth test

sources.finding: The official tutorial explicitly instructs registering http://localhost:3000.

sources.section: Authorization code grant flow; Examples of the four flows
sources.finding: Authorization and token-exchange examples use http://localhost:3000. Registered redirect URI is required.
Requires registering the application callback URL, but does not specify an HTTP localhost exception or a rule for numeric loopback IPs.

conclusion: HTTP localhost is explicitly documented. The consulted official pages did not establish whether HTTP 127.0.0.1 is accepted or forbidden. Numeric-IP support remains unverified.
implementation: Launcher local control URL now uses localhost. Session origin and derived callback therefore stay on localhost. Gateway bind and internal rendering remain on 127.0.0.1; explicit HTTPS public origin remains unchanged.
verification: 34 local boundary tests passed; 7 real-local-gateway smoke checks passed, including session/callback origin agreement. No Twitch account, token exchange or public stream was used.
